nora: Heads-up: prod linkcheck failed on /reference/sdk#python-client-usage. Fragment missing but the heading is `Python client usage (beta 🚧)` in the md. Could emoji or parentheses be changing slug?

eli: Yep. Docusaurus slugger strips emoji differently than our legacy slugify. Also parentheses and inline code ticks sometimes produce different output.

sasha: Quick reproduce: extract heading and run both sluggers

```bash
node ./scripts/extract-heading.js docs/reference/sdk.md 'Python client usage (beta 🚧)'
node ./scripts/docusaurus-slugify.js <<< "Python client usage (beta 🚧)"
node ./scripts/legacy-slugify.js <<< "Python client usage (beta 🚧)"
```

I see legacy -> "python-client-usage-beta-" and docusaurus -> "python-client-usage-beta-emoji" (it replaces emoji with name).

nora: Oof. That explains a handful of 404s reported by support after migration. Proposed fixes: 1) normalization pass removing emoji or mapping them consistently during migration; 2) generate redirect entries for migrated anchors where the slug differs; 3) add a docs CI job that compares slug outputs for PRs touching docs/* and warns on mismatches.

eli: Also suggest a short whitelist: keep parentheses and code ticks trimmed in a consistent rule set. We should add a test vector with emoji, parentheses, and backticks to prevent regressions.

sasha: I'll open a small PR with the normalization script + redirect generator and the slug-compare job. Will tag @eli for review.

docs-bot: New PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/5602 by sasha 5 add slug normalization for emoji/parentheses + slug-compare CI

deploy-bot: Docs CI (linkcheck) flagged 3 missing fragments; rerun after PR merge.
